name: Screen brightness
plain: A site cannot read how bright your screen is set.
meaning: No API exposes backlight level. Proxies: prefers-color-scheme, dynamic-range and Screen Wake Lock state. Ambient light sensor was removed from stable browsers (Chrome behind a flag, Firefox 122 removed it) for fingerprint and privacy risk.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can't see how bright your screen is set
limits.user_action: Nothing. Pages have no way to ask for this
can: See if you use light or dark mode
Check HDR and color range support
Keep your screen awake with a wake lock
Use a light sensor only where a flag turns it on in Chrome
cannot: See your battery saver or night mode
Use the ambient light sensor in Firefox, which removed it

story.what_it_is: A site cannot read how bright your screen is set.

marketing.name: Screen Wake Lock API
marketing.pitch: Chrome describes a way for a page to keep the screen on, without any control over brightness.

story.for_you: A site cannot see or change your screen brightness. It can only see whether you prefer a dark or light theme, and it can ask to keep the screen awake.
story.for_makers: Brightness is a private device setting and a possible fingerprint. The web exposes only your theme preference and wake lock. Apps work around it with themes.

use_cases.example: A video site wanted brightness to adjust the picture and uses dark or light theme instead.
A workout page keeps the screen awake during a class using wake lock.
A reading site wanted brightness to adapt contrast and relies on your theme and contrast settings.
A browser game wanted brightness for a night mode and follows the system theme.
A map in navigation mode keeps the screen on, and cannot change brightness.
An advertiser wanted brightness as a time of day clue and cannot get it.
A tracker wanted brightness as a fingerprint input and is blocked.

risks: Theme and wake lock still hint at habits

legit_uses: None: the browser deliberately withholds it
abuse: Sites attempt proxies to recover it
